fuji.get_wifistatus.note: 03 connected: the dummy WiFi is always up

fuji.get_ssid.note: SSID then the passphrase in the clear

fuji.set_ssid.note: the dummy WiFi's connect() always succeeds, so the double NAK (fwspec trap) cannot be shown on fujinet-pc

fuji.read_dir_entry.note: four exchanges: blank.h8d, disk.img, readme.txt, then 7F 7F (the end)

fuji.read_dir_entry.ext.surprise: fujinet-pc only: the details come back FF 0C 1F 12 00 00 / 00 00 00 00 / 00 / 00 (size 0, date 1969-12-31 18:00) for every entry in /test/. FileSystemSDFAT::dir_open stats <SD>/<name> instead of <SD>/<dir>/<name> (fn-h89/lib/FileSystem/fnFsSD.cpp:306), the stat fails and size/mtime stay 0; localtime() then uses the host's zone (CST), not fnconfig's timezone=UTC. The ESP32 (FatFs) path is separate code. mediatype 0 for .img matches the fwspec trap.

fuji.get_host_prefix.note: "/test"; the bytes after the NUL are uninitialized (fwspec trap)

fuji.read_device_slots.surprise: the 36-byte name is not NUL-padded: slot 0 reads 00 41 'disk.img' 00 'k.img' 00 ... - the whole path is strlcpy'd first (fn-h89/lib/device/fujiDevice/fujiDevice.cpp:1589) and the basename over its start (1601), so the tail of '/test/disk.img' survives after the NUL

fuji.mount_all.note: nothing left to mount: slot 0 was emptied by UNMOUNT_IMAGE

fuji.copy_file.note: SD /test/readme.txt -> /test/copy.txt; slots are 1-based; no host prefix set (COPY_FILE fails with one, fwspec trap)

fuji.new_disk.trap: always NAKs on this build: MediaTypeImg::create() returns an error (fn-h89/lib/media/rs232/diskTypeImg.cpp:169-172, via fn-h89/lib/device/rs232/disk.cpp:368-373); a 0-byte /test/new.h8d is left behind

fuji.unmount_host.trap: the SD host cannot be unmounted: unmount_success() is false for local hosts (fn-h89/lib/fuji/fujiHost.cpp:621-625); its drive slots are emptied before the NAK (fn-h89/lib/device/fujiDevice/fujiDevice.cpp:1553-1568)

fuji.config_boot.note: 0 with slot 0 empty: takes the boot disk out again

fuji.write_appkey.note: 16 bytes "HIGH SCORE 12345"; fujinet-lib's fuji_write_appkey() sends OPEN (mode 1) then WRITE, so the C capture has two exchanges

fuji.read_appkey.note: 10 00 then the 16 bytes; fujinet-lib's fuji_read_appkey() sends OPEN (mode 0) then READ, so the C capture has two exchanges

fuji.hash_compute.note: SHA-1 of the kept "abc", then the input is cleared

fuji.hash_output.note: a9993e364706816aba3e25717850c26c9cd0d89d = SHA-1("abc"): proves COMPUTE_NO_CLEAR kept the input

fuji.qrcode_encode.note: version 0 = smallest that fits (qrcode.c VERSION_AUTO): version 1, 21 x 21

fuji.qrcode_length.note: 40 00 00 00 = 64: a size byte, then 21 rows of 3 bytes
fuji.qrcode_length.surprise: binary and bitmap renderings start with one extra byte, the modules on a side (fn-h89/lib/qrcode/qrmanager.cpp:125,149): 64 = 1 + 21 rows x 3 bytes; fwspec's output_mode text does not mention it

fuji.qrcode_output.surprise: first byte 15H (21) is the size byte, then the rows: 15 FE A3 F8 82 FA 08 ... (see fuji.qrcode_length)

fuji.get_time.note: not dispatched on 70H: rs232Fuji's default case NAKs (fn-h89/lib/device/rs232/rs232Fuji.cpp:402-403); fujinet-lib's fuji_get_time() sends it anyway (fujinet-lib/include/fujinet-fuji.h:649)

fuji.reset.note: no ACK; fujinet-pc exits (rc 75) and the call times out after 15 s
